Artificial Neural Networks are universal function approximators, yet they suffer from local minima and require extensive hyperparameter tuning. Support Vector Machines provide strong theoretical guarantees on generalization via margin maximization, though their performance depends critically on kernel choice and regularization. All three face fundamental trade-offs between bias, variance, and computational complexity. Their predictive failures often arise from distribution shifts between training and test data, inadequate feature representation, or the inherent unpredictability of human behavior in dynamic sporting environments.
